chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Chapter 316: Li Huowang’s Costly Talisman and the Fortune at the Temple
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang visits the City God Temple to collect a debt from Blind Chen. He receives a powerful talisman manual with a sinister hidden cost. A cryptic fortune poem follows.
og_title: Chapter 316: The City God Temple — Li Huowang Collects a Debt
og_description: A quiet day in Yinling City. Li Huowang trades an Eight Trigrams Mirror for a forbidden talisman manual. The price? If he ever looks at it, he must gouge out his own eyes.
twitter_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch. 316 — Incense, Shadow-Reading, and a Hidden Face in Every Talisman
twitter_description: At the City God Temple, Li Huowang collects his reward from Blind Chen: a talisman manual that will *come alive* if he looks at it. Standard Tuesday in the Dao-Twisted World.

lore_anchors.definition: A temple dedicated to the City God (Chenghuang), a tutelary deity in Chinese folk religion who protects a city and judges the dead.
Two iconic demon guards of the Chinese underworld (Diyu), tasked with escorting the souls of the dead to judgment.
A poetic euphemism for a brothel or entertainment house in the Dao-Twisted World.
A supernatural restriction in Chinese folk magic; looking at the talisman while drawing or using it can "awaken" the spirit within, causing it to target the user.
A blind fortune-teller in Yinling City whose Eight Trigrams Mirror was stolen by a Zuowandao imposter. He repays Li Huowang's vengeance with a forbidden talisman manual.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why is Li Huowang so casual about the eye-gouging taboo?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He has endured far worse costs for power in the Dao-Twisted World. To him, a conditional threat is an acceptable risk—he is used to paying prices.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is the significance of the prostitutes at the temple?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Their presence highlights the social hopelessness of marginalized women in this feudal setting. They pray to a civic deity for basic human dignity—rescue or reincarnation as men.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Is Blind Chen's fortune poem a real prophecy?
cultural_notes_faq.a: In the Dao-Twisted World, fortune-tellers rarely speak idly. The poem likely carries a hidden meaning that will resonate with Li Huowang's future path.
